components.css: :host{--navy:#132840;--ink:#10233a;--ice:#eaf1f8;--ice-2:#dbe6f2;--gold:#e2a83c;--gold-deep:#8a5a10;--focus:#2f7fd0;--muted:#46596f;--mist:#c3d3e4;--font:-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,'Helvetica Neue',Arial,sans-serif}.ds-group{border:0;margin:0;padding:24px;background:var(--ice);color:var(--ink);font:400 17px/1.55 var(--font);max-width:380px}.ds-legend{padding:0;margin-bottom:6px;font-weight:900;text-transform:uppercase;font-size:15px;letter-spacing:.08em;color:var(--gold-deep)}.ds-row{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:14px;min-height:52px;padding:6px 0;border-bottom:1px solid var(--ice-2);cursor:pointer;font-weight:700;line-height:1.25;position:relative}.ds-row input{position:absolute;width:1px;height:1px;opacity:0;margin:0}.ds-box{flex:none;width:28px;height:28px;border-radius:8px;border:2px solid #6b819a;background:#fff;display:grid;place-items:center;transition:background-color .15s,border-color .15s,box-shadow .15s}.ds-box svg{width:16px;height:16px;opacity:0;transform:scale(.6);transition:opacity .15s,transform .2s cubic-bezier(.2,1.6,.4,1)}.ds-row:hover .ds-box{border-color:var(--focus);box-shadow:0 0 0 3px rgba(47,127,208,.22)}.ds-row input:focus-visible+.ds-box{border-color:var(--focus);box-shadow:0 0 0 3px rgba(47,127,208,.45)}.ds-row input:checked+.ds-box{background:var(--navy);border-color:var(--navy)}.ds-row input:checked+.ds-box svg{opacity:1;transform:none}.ds-sub{display:block;font-weight:500;font-size:15px;color:var(--muted)}

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Wiped Winter Window"**

The page is a frosted window at winter dusk. Navy bands are glass with a dark street behind them: rooftops, a few gold-lit windows, snow on the ground. Frost ferns grow in from the edges and the visitor wipes them away with a finger or cursor. Meltwater drops run down the cleared glass, and the frost slowly grows back. Between the glass panes sit pale ice reading bands where the real content lives: the full service list, the steps, the discounts. The metaphor matches the job. T&M leaves a house empty, clean and ready for the cold, and the page lets you clear the glass the same way.

The pacing is dense and plain. Big, heavy, uppercase system-sans headlines, short first-person copy in William's voice, and one gold call to action per screen. Decoration only comes from the winter world: frost, drops, snowdrift and icicle seams. There are no stock photos, icon-card grids or review carousels. The page is a working tool (tick jobs, send a text), and the weather around it is the personality.

Rejected outright: a black ground (the flyer's black panel does not carry over), cards for services, and any warm accent other than the flyer's gold.
keyCharacteristics: Navy dusk glass bands alternate with ice reading bands, separated by animated SVG snowdrift and icicle seams, never by straight lines.
The frost-wipe canvas is the signature element. Every navy pane carries one, and text always sits on glass that is already clear.
Heavy uppercase system sans (900) for every heading. The owner chose this house style on purpose.
Gold is trim only: the lit phone number, the primary pill button, the ampersand, the second hero line, step numbers and check ticks.
Services appear as one long ticked list grouped under three plain labels, and the selection becomes a pre-filled text message.

rules.name: The Never-Black Rule
rules.body: The darkest ground is Winter Dusk Navy. No surface, band or overlay goes to black or near-neutral grey. Dark means dusk, not night.

rules.name: The Gold-Is-Light Rule
rules.body: Gold shows up as small lit things (a number, a pill, a tick, a lit window) and never as a band or large field. If gold covers more of a screen than the primary button does, it has stopped being trim.

rules.name: The Two-Rings Rule
rules.body: Focus is gold on navy and Frost Blue on ice. Never put a gold ring on an ice ground.

rules.name: The Weight-Not-Face Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy comes from size and weight in a single system stack. Do not add a second family.

rules.name: The Shouting-Stops-At-Headings Rule
rules.body: Uppercase belongs to headings, the wordmark and group legends. Buttons, list items and prose stay in sentence case, in William's voice.

rules.name: The Clear-Glass Rule
rules.body: Text on a pane never relies on its halo alone. The frost mask is cleared around every `[data-clear]` element's line boxes and buttons, so copy always sits on clear glass and the halo is the backup.

rules.name: The Halo-Matches-Ground Rule
rules.body: Text halos use the ground color they protect (navy on glass, ice on frost), never an accent.

dos: Do alternate dusk-glass panes and ice reading bands, and join every glass-to-ice change with a seam (snowdrift when leaving a pane, icicle eave when entering one).
Do give every new navy pane the frost-wipe canvas and mark its copy and buttons `data-clear` so the frost stays off them.
Do set headings in the system stack at 900, uppercase, line-height 1.02, -0.01em tracking.
Do keep gold to small lit elements: one gold pill per screen, the phone number, the ampersand, step numerals, ticks.
Do use the gold focus ring on navy and the Frost Blue (#2f7fd0) ring on ice.
Do make every contact action a real `tel:` or `sms:` link with a pre-filled body, at least 56px tall for buttons and 44px for links, with tabular figures on numbers.
Do put text halos in the ground color (navy on glass, ice on frost) and honor `prefers-reduced-motion` by drawing frost and seams once at rest.
donts: Don't use black or neutral grey as a ground. The darkest surface is Winter Dusk Navy (#132840).
Don't use gold as a band, large field or body-text color on ice. Use Burnt Gold (#8a5a10) where gold-family text has to sit on ice.
Don't show services as icon cards or tiles. They are one ticked list under plain group labels.
Don't separate bands with straight rules or hard color cuts where a seam belongs.
Don't add a second typeface or a webfont. The system stack is the house style.
Don't add stock photos, invented before/afters, reviews or a logo mark. The world comes from the frost scene, and the name is set as a wordmark.
Don't set buttons, list items or prose in uppercase.
